slides: Short wedding vows: a few honest lines can carry as much weight as a long speech.
Our advice: 1 to 2 minutes at most. Don't count words. Read yours aloud, with pauses, and time it on your phone.
"I will listen. I will laugh with you, often. And I will show up every day, especially the hard ones."
Five parts are enough: a name, one specific memory, two or three promises, a small habit you love and a closing line.
One memory, not a history. Promises you can keep. End on a short line, because the last words are the ones guests hear.
Outdoors, wind and waves swallow voices. Ask your venue about a microphone and test it at the rehearsal.
In Australia, your own vows sit alongside the words the law asks you to say. Ask your celebrant how they fit together.
Marrying far from home? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Some couples want to speak for five minutes. Others would rather say something true, say it well and hand the moment back to the ceremony.

Our new guide, Short Wedding Vows Examples Under One Minute, has 20 original examples grouped by tone: classic, romantic, modern and simple, light and funny, for him, for her, for a destination ceremony and for a renewal. Each one is yours to adapt.

A few lines from the list:
"I promise you the long view. Not only today, with everyone dressed up and the light just right, but the Tuesday nights, the airport queues and the years our hair turns grey."
"Our dog approved of you before I did, and she has excellent judgement."
"The first time, I hoped. This time, I know."

How to keep yours short:
- Aim for 1 to 2 minutes at most. Read it aloud at the pace you would use in front of guests and time it.
- One memory, not a history. A road trip or a burnt dinner says more than a timeline.
- Make promises you can keep. "I will make the coffee on weekdays" beats a promise about the stars.
- Agree on a similar length with your partner, and share both with your celebrant before the day.

In Australia, your own words sit alongside the words the law asks you to say, so ask your celebrant how they fit together. If you marry legally overseas, the legal wording follows that country.

Marrying far from home? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
